title: Doppler ultrasound in pregnancy
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to see how blood flows in the umbilical cord and in the vessels of the uterus and the baby. It shows if the baby gets enough nutrients and oxygen.
why: Often with screening in the 2nd and 3rd trimesters. More often if the baby is small, or with high blood pressure, diabetes, or twins.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; results right away
tell_doctor: How many weeks pregnant you are
If your blood pressure is high or you have swelling
If you have diabetes or kidney disease
How the baby has been moving in the last few days

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: Usually none. You can eat, and you do not need a full bladder.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, so your belly is easy to uncover.

steps: You lie on your back or slightly on your side
Gel is put on your belly
The doctor finds the cord and vessels with the probe
Blood flow mode is turned on. You may hear the sound of the blood vessels
The doctor takes measurements in several vessels
feel: Cool gel and light pressure on your belly
Lying on your back can make you dizzy. Tell the doctor, and you will be turned on your side
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
If the results are not normal, the doctor will decide on a repeat scan or closer checks
red_flags: The baby moves much less or has stopped moving: see a doctor right away or call emergency services
Bleeding, belly pain, or your water breaking: call emergency services

faq.q: Is Doppler harmful to the baby?
faq.a: No. When there is a medical reason, it is considered safe. It is done briefly and only as needed.

faq.q: What is the sound during the Doppler?
faq.a: It is the sound of blood in the vessels and the baby's heartbeat.

reminders.text: Pregnancy Doppler tomorrow. No prep needed. Bring your pregnancy record.
